content.title: A look at Kentucky basketball head coach Mark Pope
content.text: Kentucky coaches Mark Pope, Mark Fox and Nick Robinson before a loss to Vanderbilt, 74-69. Photo by Chet White. Saturday, January 25, 2025. The No. 8 Vols will host the No. 12 Wildcats on Tuesday, but this matchup is different from years past. For the first time in 15 years, John Calipari will not be the Wildcats’ head coach. Mark Pope took over as Kentucky’s coach in April 2024 after Calipari left for Arkansas. If Pope’s name sounds familiar to long-time Vols fans, it’s for good reason. He played for the Wildcats in the mid-1990s. Pope played in every game from 1994-96 for Kentucky under head coach Rick Pitino. He was part of the 1996 NCAA National Championship team and won two SEC titles before being drafted into the NBA. Pope’s hiring as head coach wasn’t based on his playing career, however. Before coming to Kentucky, he was the head coach at BYU for five seasons. In his first year with BYU, Pope led the Cougars to as high as No. 14 in the AP Poll in 2019 and won a conference game against No. 2 Gonzaga. His first season was cut short by the COVID-19 pandemic, preventing him from securing an NCAA Tournament win. That season remained his best shot at a tournament victory at BYU. Pope took the Cougars to the Tournament in 2021 and 2024 but lost in the first round both times. Now, in his first season with Kentucky, Pope has led the Wildcats to a 14-5 record. He has impressive wins over Duke — who is now ranked second in the country — Florida, Mississippi State and Texas A&M. Pope has had some questionable losses this season as only one of them was against a ranked Alabama squad. Kentucky lost to Vanderbilt in its most recent game and suffered a 13-point loss to Georgia. Pope’s other two losses were earlier in the season before conference play began. The Wildcats fell four points short against Clemson for their first loss of the year. Their second loss is the most surprising, as Kentucky lost by 20 points against Ohio State on Dec. 21 — doubling down on wins for the Buckeyes in basketball and football that day. After losing his third conference game, in a game which Kentucky committed 17 turnovers, Pope gave praise to the level of defense in the SEC. “I mean everybody’s really good defensively, right,” Pope said. “That’s the great thing about this league.” Pope’s offense can score. The Wildcats rank third in Division I in points per game, despite facing SEC defenses. Kentucky doesn’t rely on one player to carry the scoring load — five Wildcats average more than 10 points per game, and one averages 9.7. The Vols are not just a “really good” defensive team, as Pope put it — they are the best defensive team in the SEC. Compared to the rest of Division I, Tennessee ranks third in scoring defense, allows the second-lowest field goal percentage and allows the lowest three-point percentage. The No. 8 Vols will look to remain undefeated at home and extend the losing streak of Pope’s No. 12 Wildcats to three games. The loser of this matchup will drop to four conference losses.
